analysis:
Only base-side text of docs/developer/build.md (lines 1-950) was supplied for these two units. No patch hunk or head text was included, so I could not identify what changed. I raised no findings.

Security-relevant statements in the base text that a later pass should compare against the diff:
- Line 249: the release pipeline registers the exact signed official build through the scoped `POST /v1/releases`, after platform persistence is deployed. No per-release hardware qualification or manual approval is required. This ties to A-005, A-011, A-017, T-054, T-024 and T-025.
- Lines 251-255: secret-bearing release jobs accept only verified signed annotated tags in reviewed `master` ancestry, or trusted `master` for dev/manual/recovery runs. They use repository-scoped secrets and need no environment approval. They assume trusted repository writers, and CI establishes official identity, not runtime Apple success.
- Lines 326-329 and 358-365: protected signing and publication jobs keep their approvals, credential scopes and same-run artifact checks. Release-plumbing PRs run with PR-scoped caches and no signing or publishing secrets.
- Lines 387-388: only unsigned build directories are cached, never signing keys or notarized bundles.
- Lines 97-116: pinned installer and GitHub CLI SHA-256 verification.
- Lines 263-275: Bedrock threat-review workflow with hash-locked dependencies and a separate read-only org-membership token.
- Line 243: App Attest shadow packaging is a separate acceptance step from a successful local compile.

Coverage limit: any weakening of these controls in the head revision, such as approvals, cache scopes, secret exposure, hash pinning or the release-registration flow, cannot be assessed from base-only text. Integration should check later units for the actual patch before treating this as clean.
